data.title: Wifi Issue
data.description:
The new iPhone 11 Pro has a new wireless firmware that can support up to 7GHz of wireless bandwidth speed. This gives the users unmatched speed in comparison to most of the smartphones in the market. However, there have been issues regarding the Wi-Fi of the iPhone 11 pro. And frankly, some users have taken issue with the phone saying that the phone disconnects from the wireless network frequently and without any warning.

Other issues like high ping or latency have often been reported by the users of the phone. The most common reported iPhone 11 Pro Wi-Fi issues are…

  • Wi-Fi gets disconnected on iPhone 11 pro.
  • Wi-Fi stays connected but there is no internet on the receiver.
  • Slow Wi-Fi speeds on metered/ non-metered connections on Wi-Fi.
  • High Latency/Ping on Wi-Fi connections
  • iPhone fails to connect to Wi-Fi
  • iPhone can’t discover your Wi-Fi connection.

These Wi-Fi issues found on iPhone 11 pro are pretty common issues found on other wireless supported devices too! And does not necessarily indicate that there is something specifically wrong with your iPhone 11 pro’s wireless hardware. There are some DIY(Do it yourself) fixes available for your smartphone in this case.

  • Check your wireless router. Unplug it from the power source for 10 minutes and try again and see if the issues have been resolved.
  • Turn your Wi-Fi off for five minutes and try again.
  • Forget and reconnect your Wi-Fi connection.
  • Restore the default network connection
  • ( Reset from here: Settings > General > Reset > Reset Network Connections > * Enter Passcode * > Confirm)
  • Update your iOS to the latest version available.

If none of the solutions mentioned above works to resolve your Wi-Fi issues on your iPhone 11 pro, you may need to get it checked by a professional technician. Signs You Might Need to Replace the Taptic Engine:

If your iPhone stops providing vibrations or feedback for notifications, calls, or system interactions.

The Taptic Engine works only occasionally or inconsistently.

The Taptic Engine produces grinding or buzzing noises that were not present before.

Error messages or diagnostics indicate an issue with the Taptic Engine.

Possible Causes of Failure:

Physical Damage: Dropping the phone or exposing it to water can damage internal components.

Software Bugs: Sometimes, a software issue may mimic hardware failure. Perform a factory reset or update the iPhone before deciding on hardware repair.

Wear and Tear: Over time, mechanical components can degrade and stop working properly.

data.title: Charge Draining Issue
data.description:
The battery is optimized perfectly for the phone. However, it may be for some manufacturer error or something about some faulty apps’ optimization, you may not get the smoothest output from your iPhone 11 pro battery. Most users have reported that the iPhone’s battery starts draining after the system has updated to iOS 14 Several other issues may cause battery drain issues also. These issues include:

  • The battery of the iPhone 11 pro runs out too quickly after the update
  • The battery of the iPhone 11 pro runs out after installing an app/ update of an app
  • The battery of the iPhone drains quickly after turning on the optimized charging mode
  • The iPhone Battery drains after the phone heats up too quickly

These are the most common problems regarding battery-draining found on the internet. Your issues may be one of them or not listed! However, we recommend trying some DIY (Do it yourself) fixes that may resolve your issue.

  • Turn off background iCloud/iTunes sync to save battery by a considerable amount
  • When not in use turn off WiFi/Cellular Data/Location/Bluetooth service in your iPhone
  • Don’t overcharge/ Frequently charge your iPhone 11 pro. It may reduce battery health
  • Turn on optimized battery charging to save your battery life and protect it from draining
  • Adjust your brightness settings in iPhone 11 pro to auto-brightness
  • Turn off Background app refresh
  • From here: Settings > general > Background app refresh
  • Try running it on low power mode
  • from here: Settings > Battery > Low power mode ON
  • Turn off “reduce motion” to turn off aesthetic animations in your phone to save battery life might help
  • Turn it off from here: Settings > General > Accessibility > Reduce Motion

If none of the aforementioned procedures work to resolve your battery draining issues, it may need to be looked at by a professional technician to get them resolved. data.title: Error Solution
data.description:
Sometimes when you update your iPhone, or when you try to run your phone you may see some sort of black screen with some sort of Error with a number on your iPhone’s screen out of nowhere. These messages with errors and numbers can be seen while booting up the phone or trying to upgrade the ipsw files from iTunes from a pc. These are Error Codes that indicate to the service technicians that a specific part of the iPhone is malfunctioning. These codes are used by professional repair technicians of iPhones to make their jobs easy.

They do not need to diagnose the entire iPhone when they see the code. Therefore saves both the customer’s and the tech expert’s time and other resources.

Some of the common error codes seen in the iPhones are as follows:

ERROR(9): This code shows when you are trying to upgrade your iOS through PC on iTunes, but the iTunes app shows an Error code-9. It is a relatable problem with iTunes error codes – 4013, 4014, and 4005.

Apple recommends:

To check if your iPhone is updated

To check if the lightning cable works. (Error code 4013,4014 and 4015 usually indicate this issue)

If the update still fails try updating from another pc

Error 1015: This is an issue if you have a jailbroken device (iOS) and apple detects it.

Error 69: This is a common issue found in iPhone X and later devices. This issue suggests that there might be some sort of hardware error on your phone, which is repairable, to say the least.

Aside from these errors, there are a lot of errors that can occur on your iPhone. These are all listed on Apple’s error solution info pages with possible DIY (Do it yourself) solutions.

Make sure your touchscreen protector doesn’t interfere with proper operation.

Make sure there’s no internal/external damage (cracking or shattering glass).

Disconnect your USB-lightning port to check if it works.

If your phone is above normal temperature, wait for it to cool down and then try again.

Restart your device.

data.title: Liquid Damage
data.description:
The new iPhone 11 Pro is a standard IP68-rated, dust- and water-resistant phone. This means it can resist dust and water coming in up to a certain level. However, it is not completely immune to water getting inside the iPhone and damaging it. Apple has introduced a new technology called LCI. LCI is an abbreviation for liquid contact indicator. It is located in the SIM tray region. Now you can see the LCI when you remove the SIM tray by putting the ejector pin into the SIM tray ejection hole. Once you have removed the SIM tray, you should see a white/red portion inside the SIM tray region. That is your LCI on the iPhone. If the LCI is completely white or silver, then it is okay. The phone hasn’t contacted any water.

However, if your LCI turns red, you can safely assume that it has been in touch with water and has taken in some water damage. If you have dropped your phone in the water, here are some basic things you should do:

  • Rinse your phone with a lens cloth or a microfiber cloth.
  • You may gently tap the phone with the charger hole against your hand. It may drip the water out if it has gotten in there.
  • NEVER CHARGE YOUR PHONE UNTIL YOU HAVE MADE SURE IT IS COMPLETELY DRY.
  • If anything spills on your phone (like oil, etc.), just rinse the place with a lint-free cloth.
  • If water has gotten into your phone , it may damage your battery or charging port or give you muffled speakers.

data.title: Stuck On Logo
data.description:
The new iPhone 11 Pro offers its users better optimization and balance in software than the previous iPhone models. However, no matter hard they try there can always be some technical issues that can result in your iPhone malfunctioning. The Apple logo stuck issue was also found in previous iPhones and it’s a frustrating issue. Your iPhone boots up, but instead of going to the home screen, it is stuck on the boot menu.

This problem happens mainly/most of the time because of a software issue that happens due to an unclean or interrupted update.

  • This Stuck on Apple logo issue might happen in other instances too. Possible reasons might be:
  • The iPhone has taken in some physical damage. (Dropping from hand)
  • Update was disrupted due to Wi-Fi disturbance/metered connection or cellular data loss
  • A third-party app may have access to vital permissions that can disrupt iPhones' productivity
  • It is rare; however, your phone might be facing a hardware issue. Sometimes faulty hardware prevents the phone from booting up

These issues however can be resolved if it is just a bug or a glitch in the iOS software. You may try the following steps and see if it works for you.

Force Restart your iPhone 11 pro

(Press volume up (+) and then quickly press volume down (-) button and hold the iPhone 11 pro power button as long as the apple logo appears again)

Update your iOS Software. (If, while in the progress of updating your software, the progress bar under the Apple logo has not moved for an hour, you may connect your iPhone to a PC and select “Update” when prompted)

Remove all third-party apps from your phone. Install Apps only from the Apple App store

Turn off the auto-update of your iOS apps to prevent further interruptions. BUT BE SURE TO UPDATE THEM ON A REGULAR BASIS MANUALLY.

data.description:
The new iPhone 11 Pro comes with a distinct feature named Face ID. Where it uses the iPhone user's face to unlock the phone. This feature was made available from the iPhone X models and the later Apple A12x Bionic chipsets. The Face ID feature uses the true depth, dual front cameras provided with the iPhone as the basic instrument for this feature. It also emits an infrared laser to convert your distinct and unique facial features into geometrical and mathematical data for the iPhone.

Face ID is a very complex technology, and users might often misinterpret one of its features as an error in the technology. Here are some common issues regarding the iPhone’s Face ID feature...

Face not recognized

Face ID is not available at the moment

Move the camera a bit lower/higher

Upon Unlocking iPhone directly takes me into Passcode and not Face ID

These common issues however have some home remedies which may work for your iPhone. These fix attempts are risk-free and do not risk damaging your phone.

Check if your face ID is on for iPhone Unlock. Go to: Settings > Face ID and Passcode

If you use a screen protector make sure it doesn’t obstruct the front camera in any way

Make sure you face the camera and nothing is covering or obstructing between your face and camera region

Restart your phone. Make sure there is no dirt or your front camera lens is not foggy

Update your iOS to the latest version

If your phone doesn’t unlock with Face ID instead prompts with a passcode. The reasons may be:

User might be wearing a face mask while opening the iPhone

The user may have just restarted the device

The phone has not been unlocked in more than 48 hours

The passcode has not been used to unlock the phone in the last 7 days

The device has not been unlocked by face ID in the last 4 hours

The iPhone has a remote lock on and is away from safe space

If a user fails to unlock the device after five unsuccessful face ID unlock attempts.

If at Face ID set up, your iPhone shows or tells you to move the device lower or higher. data.title: Software Issue
data.description:
The new iPhone 11 Pro is one of the most elegant phones on the market, which is based on iOS, a very optimized software, and sits perfectly with the specifications that Apple provides in their handsets. Initially, iPhone released a new version of iOS and updated it later to fix and patch bugs and security weaknesses from the previous versions. However, some users have reported common problems regarding iPhone 11 Pro software, which may indicate there may be a bug or some sort of error on your end that can be fixed. But the problems are unique and have to be fixed manually. Apple releases updates to fix problems that are only found in all devices.

Users in Apple’s forum reported some common problems that are listed below...

  • Battery health drop after upgrading to iOS 14.1
  • The App Store crashes after upgrading.
  • The iPhone freezes and doesn’t turn on.
  • Stuck on the activation screen/stuck on loading or Apple logo
  • iPhone stuck on “Hello” screen
  • The iPhone 11 Pro frequently restarts
  • Error 69 on iPhone update
  • Stuck on boot/boot-loop issues on iPhone 11 Pro

Some users have reported other problems with similar symptoms on their phones, which loosely qualify under the iPhone 11 Pro’s software issues. Some users think that the no signal/no Wi-Fi problem falls under the “software issues” category, but it is a separate issue that requires a separate mode of service.
